title: What might have been
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: congiuntivo trapassato, new here, in the se half only: avessi or fossi plus a participle
condizionale passato, new here, in the other half: avrei or sarei plus a participle
imperfetto, L2-M10's, for the spoken dovevo and potevo shortcut
passato prossimo, L2-M10's, in the clause after meno male che

rules.text: THE MACHINE IS TWO COMPOUND HALVES AND NOTHING IN IT IS NEW BUT THE ORDER. se plus avessi or fossi plus a participle in the first half, avrei or sarei plus a participle in the second: Se avessi saputo, avrei chiamato. The auxiliary law is L2-M10's (avere for most verbs, essere for going and coming and staying), the participles are L3-M10's, the endings -ei, -esti, -ebbe are L3-M4's. What is new is only this: the AUXILIARY now carries the tense and the main verb stops moving. Two forms to learn, not fifty.

THE TENSE GOES INTO THE MODAL, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF ENGLISH. English keeps should and could in the present and moves the perfect behind them — I should have gone. Italian moves the tense into the modal itself: avrei dovuto andare, avrei potuto dire, avrei voluto venire, with the infinitive left bare at the end. dovrei essere andato is not Italian. Only avere is used under a modal here; the essere version is a later rung's.

se IS COMPULSORY. English can drop if by inverting the auxiliary — Had I known, I would have called — and Italian has no such move at all. The se half also never takes a conditional: Se avrei saputo is the single commonest learner error in this frame. Conditional on the RIGHT of the comma, congiuntivo on the left, always.

avessi LOOKS LIKE avevo AND IS NOT ONE. L2-M10's avevo is the imperfetto and states a fact about the past; avessi states something that did not happen. The minimal pair is worth saying aloud: Se avevo tempo, venivo — what a speaker actually says in relaxed speech, per L3-M4 — against Se avessi avuto tempo, sarei venuto, which is the careful form and the one this module teaches.

THE REGRET WORDS ARE SHORT AND THEY CARRY THE FEELING. che peccato is what a shame, meno male che is just as well, magari plus avessi is if only, altrimenti is otherwise, invece di plus an infinitive is instead of. Beside them sits the spoken shortcut: dovevo chiamare and potevo dire are heard constantly for the full avrei dovuto and avrei potuto, and both are ordinary speech rather than sloppiness.

sentences.display: Se avessi saputo, ti avrei chiamato
sentences.cue: If I had known, I would have called you
sentences.literal: If I-had known, you I-would-have called

words.note: The participle of sapere, and irregular: sapere gives saputo, not sapito. Se avessi saputo on its own is a whole sentence of regret.

words.cue: I would have, as the auxiliary
words.note: L3-M4's conditional endings on avere. It carries the tense; the verb behind it is a participle and never changes: avrei chiamato, avresti chiamato, avrebbe chiamato.

sentences.trap: avessi is not L2-M10's avevo. avevo says it was so; avessi says it was not. Se avevo saputo is heard in relaxed speech, but it says a different thing from what you mean here.
sentences.sound: se a-VES-see sa-POO-to, tee av-RAY kya-MA-to. avessi has a double s and both are held; avrei is two syllables, av-RAY, with the stress at the end.

variations.display: Se avessi saputo, ti avrei scritto
variations.cue: If I had known, I would have written to you
variations.changed: scritto for chiamato, same machine

variations.display: Se lo avessi saputo, ti avrei chiamato
variations.cue: If I had known it, I would have called you
variations.changed: lo added, so the thing known is named

variations.display: Se avessi saputo, sarei venuto
variations.cue: If I had known, I would have come
variations.changed: sarei for avrei, because venire takes essere

mistake.display: Se avrei saputo, ti avrei chiamato
mistake.why: The conditional never goes in the se half. se takes avessi; avrei belongs on the other side of the comma. This is the error to unlearn first.

sentences.usage: Apologising for something you did not do because nobody told you.
sentences.mnemonic: avessi on the left, avrei on the right.

sentences.display: Avrei dovuto dire la verità subito
sentences.cue: I should have told the truth straight away
sentences.literal: I-would-have had-to to-say the truth immediately

words.note: One block, then a bare infinitive. English moves the perfect behind should; Italian moves it into the modal. Never dovrei essere andato.
Irregular and very short. Its participle detto is L3-M5's, so dire is the infinitive half of a verb the course already half owns.
Feminine and invariable: la verità, le verità. The final accent is stressed, ve-ri-TA, and it never changes for plural.

sentences.trap: dovuto here is not I owed. Under avrei it is the should of hindsight, and the thing you should have done follows as a plain infinitive with nothing between them.
sentences.sound: av-RAY do-VOO-to DEE-re la ve-ri-TA SOO-bee-to. verità ends on the stressed a; subito is stressed on the first syllable, SOO-bee-to.

variations.display: Avresti dovuto dire la verità subito
variations.cue: You should have told the truth straight away
variations.changed: avresti, so it is said to somebody else

variations.display: Dovevo dire la verità subito
variations.cue: I should have told the truth straight away
variations.changed: the spoken shortcut, dovevo for avrei dovuto

variations.display: Avrei dovuto dire la verità prima
variations.cue: I should have told the truth earlier
variations.changed: prima for subito, so it is about timing

mistake.display: Dovrei aver detto la verità subito
mistake.why: This is English word for word and Italian does not say it. The tense lives in the modal: avrei dovuto dire, one block, then the bare infinitive.

sentences.usage: Owning up, after the fact, to having held something back.
sentences.mnemonic: The tense climbs into the modal.

sentences.cue: It would have been better to leave yesterday

words.note: L3-M4's sarebbe plus essere's own participle stato. Impersonal here, so it stays masculine singular and an infinitive follows.

sentences.trap: No se is needed. Sarebbe stato meglio states the better option on its own, and English would have been better works the same way — the if half is simply left unsaid.
sentences.sound: sa-REB-be STA-to MEL-yo par-TEE-re YE-ree. meglio is MEL-yo, the gli sound, not meg-lee-o.

variations.display: Sarebbe stato meglio partire prima
variations.cue: It would have been better to leave earlier
variations.changed: prima for ieri, so it is relative and not a date

variations.display: Sarebbe stato meglio restare a casa
variations.cue: It would have been better to stay at home
variations.changed: the opposite choice, restare for partire

variations.display: Sarebbe stato meglio non partire
variations.cue: It would have been better not to leave
variations.changed: non before the infinitive, negating the advice

mistake.display: Sarebbe stato meglio sono partito ieri
mistake.why: After meglio the verb is an infinitive, never a conjugated tense: partire, not sono partito. Italian keeps the infinitive where English keeps to leave.

sentences.usage: Saying, after a bad trip, what the right call would have been.
sentences.mnemonic: Better + to-do: meglio takes an infinitive.

sentences.cue: If only I had listened to my mother

words.note: Regular -are, so the participle is ascoltato. It takes its object directly: ascoltare mia madre, with no word for to.

sentences.trap: L3-M3's magari means maybe. In front of avessi it changes job entirely and means if only, and the wish is always one that did not come true.
sentences.sound: ma-GA-ree a-VES-see as-kol-TA-to MEE-a MA-dre. magari is stressed in the middle, ma-GA-ree.

variations.display: Magari avessi ascoltato mio padre
variations.cue: If only I had listened to my father
variations.changed: mio padre, so the possessive agrees the other way

variations.display: Magari avessi ascoltato prima
variations.cue: If only I had listened earlier
variations.changed: no object, just the timing

variations.display: Avrei dovuto ascoltare mia madre
variations.cue: I should have listened to my mother
variations.changed: the regret said flat, without the wish

mistake.why: With the passato prossimo, magari goes back to meaning maybe and the sentence says I may have listened. The wish reading needs avessi.

sentences.usage: The wish you say out loud when the advice you ignored turns out to have been right.

sentences.display: Meno male che ho portato l'ombrello
sentences.cue: Just as well I brought the umbrella
sentences.literal: Less bad that I-have brought the-umbrella

words.note: Literally less bad. The relief version of a regret, and the clause after it is an ordinary passato prossimo. Drop the che and meno male stands alone.
Regular -are. portare covers both bringing and wearing, so ho portato l'ombrello and porto gli occhiali use one verb.
Masculine, so l'ombrello with the elided article. The apostrophe is part of the word here: l'ombrello is written and said as one piece.

sentences.trap: meno male is not less bad in any literal sense. It is the standard thank goodness, and it is said about small things all day long.
sentences.sound: ME-no MA-le ke o por-TA-to lom-BREL-lo. l'ombrello runs together as lom-BREL-lo, with no pause at the apostrophe.

variations.display: Meno male che hai portato l'ombrello
variations.cue: Just as well you brought the umbrella
variations.changed: hai, so the relief is about somebody else

variations.display: Meno male, ho portato l'ombrello
variations.cue: Just as well — I brought the umbrella
variations.changed: che dropped, so meno male stands alone

variations.display: Meno male che ho portato gli ombrelli
variations.cue: Just as well I brought the umbrellas
variations.changed: the plural, gli ombrelli

mistake.why: When a whole clause follows, che is not optional: Meno male CHE ho portato. Bare meno male works only as a standalone exclamation.

sentences.usage: Said with relief when the thing you nearly forgot turns out to have been needed.

sentences.display: Se fossi partito prima, non avrei perso il treno
sentences.cue: If I had left earlier, I would not have missed the train
sentences.literal: If I-were left earlier, not I-would-have lost the train

words.cue: I had, as the auxiliary for essere verbs
words.note: The essere half of the se machine. It is used wherever L2-M10 used sono: partito, venuto, rimasto. The participle then agrees — fossi partito, fossi partita.
Joins a fact to what would have followed without it: Sono partito prima, altrimenti avrei perso il treno. The half after it stays conditional.

sentences.trap: The auxiliary choice is L2-M10's and nothing here changes it. partire took essere in the passato prossimo, so it takes fossi here, and its participle still agrees with the speaker.
sentences.sound: se FOS-see par-TEE-to PREE-ma, non av-RAY PER-so il TRE-no. fossi has the double s held, FOS-see.

variations.display: Sono partito prima, altrimenti avrei perso il treno
variations.cue: I left earlier — otherwise I would have missed the train
variations.changed: the fact stated, and altrimenti carrying the rest

variations.display: Se fossi partita prima, non avrei perso il treno
variations.cue: If I had left earlier, I would not have missed the train
variations.changed: partita, so a woman is speaking

variations.display: Se fossimo partiti prima, non avremmo perso il treno
variations.cue: If we had left earlier, we would not have missed the train
variations.changed: both halves in the we form

mistake.display: Se avessi partito prima, non avrei perso il treno
mistake.why: partire is an essere verb, so the se half takes fossi and not avessi. The auxiliary law does not change just because the tense did.

sentences.usage: Working out afterwards exactly where the morning went wrong.
sentences.mnemonic: essere verbs keep essere: fossi partito.

sentences.display: Avrei potuto dire qualcosa, ma non ho detto niente
sentences.cue: I could have said something, but I said nothing
sentences.literal: I-would-have been-able to-say something, but not I-have said nothing

words.note: Same block as avrei dovuto, with potere inside it. A bare infinitive follows: avrei potuto dire, avrei potuto venire.
Needs non before the verb: non ho detto niente. The double negative is compulsory in Italian, not an error. nulla is the tidier written twin.
The imperfetto standing in for avrei potuto. Extremely common in speech and it means the same reproach: Potevo dire qualcosa.
The imperfetto of volere. It states the intention that came to nothing, which is why it sits with regrets: Volevo dire qualcosa.
The third modal block. Softer than avrei dovuto: it reports a wish rather than an obligation you failed.

sentences.trap: non ho detto niente is not a double negative to be fixed. Italian keeps both halves, and dropping non leaves the sentence ungrammatical rather than emphatic.
sentences.sound: av-RAY po-TOO-to DEE-re kwal-KO-sa, ma non o DET-to NYEN-te. niente is two syllables, NYEN-te.

variations.display: Potevo dire qualcosa, ma non ho detto niente
variations.cue: I could have said something, but I said nothing
variations.changed: the spoken potevo for avrei potuto

variations.display: Avrei voluto dire qualcosa, ma non ho detto niente
variations.cue: I would have liked to say something, but I said nothing
variations.changed: voluto for potuto: a wish, not an ability

variations.display: Volevo dire qualcosa, ma non ho detto niente
variations.cue: I wanted to say something, but I said nothing
variations.changed: volevo, the intention stated flat

mistake.display: Avrei potuto dire qualcosa, ma ho detto niente
mistake.why: niente still needs its non: non ho detto niente. Italian never drops the non when the negative word comes after the verb.

sentences.usage: Admitting you stayed quiet in a meeting when you should not have.
sentences.mnemonic: niente always brings non with it.

sentences.display: Che peccato, sarebbe stato un bel viaggio
sentences.cue: What a shame, it would have been a lovely trip
sentences.literal: What shame, it-would-be been a nice trip

words.note: One block, with no article: never che un peccato. It is the ordinary reaction to bad news, small or large.
The noun on its own, said as a whole reaction: Peccato! It also means sin, but nobody hears that reading in this use.
Masculine, double g said as one soft sound: VYAD-jo. Buon viaggio is what you say to somebody leaving.

sentences.trap: che peccato takes no article, unlike English what A shame. Adding one gives che un peccato, which is not said.
sentences.sound: ke pek-KA-to, sa-REB-be STA-to un bel VYAD-jo. peccato holds the double c, pek-KA-to.

variations.display: Peccato, sarebbe stato un bel viaggio
variations.cue: Shame — it would have been a lovely trip
variations.changed: che dropped, leaving the bare noun

variations.display: Che peccato, sarebbe stato un bel giorno
variations.cue: What a shame, it would have been a lovely day
variations.changed: giorno for viaggio

variations.display: Che peccato, avrei voluto fare quel viaggio
variations.cue: What a shame, I would have liked to take that trip
variations.changed: the regret made personal with avrei voluto

mistake.display: Che un peccato, sarebbe stato un bel viaggio
mistake.why: che peccato carries no article. English needs what A shame; Italian puts the noun straight after che.

sentences.usage: Reacting to a cancelled plan somebody has just told you about.

sentences.display: Dovevo partire ieri, invece sono rimasto a casa
sentences.cue: I was supposed to leave yesterday, but instead I stayed at home
sentences.literal: I-had-to to-leave yesterday, instead I-am stayed at home

words.note: The imperfetto of dovere. It reports a plan that did not happen, and in speech it stands in for avrei dovuto without sounding careless.
Opens the half that actually happened. It sits at the front of its clause and needs no di when a whole clause follows.
The same word with di, and then a bare infinitive: invece di partire. Never invece di sono partito.

sentences.trap: invece and invece di are not interchangeable. Bare invece takes a clause; invece di takes an infinitive, and mixing them is the commonest slip in this pair.
sentences.sound: do-VE-vo par-TEE-re YE-ree, in-VE-che SO-no ree-MA-sto a KA-sa. invece has the soft c, in-VE-che.

variations.display: Invece di partire, sono rimasto a casa
variations.cue: Instead of leaving, I stayed at home
variations.changed: invece di plus the infinitive, fronted

variations.display: Avrei dovuto partire ieri, invece sono rimasto a casa
variations.cue: I should have left yesterday, but instead I stayed at home
variations.changed: the full avrei dovuto for the spoken dovevo

variations.display: Doveva partire ieri, invece è rimasto a casa
variations.cue: He was supposed to leave yesterday, but instead he stayed at home
variations.changed: the whole line moved to the he form

mistake.display: Dovevo partire ieri, invece di sono rimasto a casa
mistake.why: invece di must be followed by an infinitive. Before a full clause the word is bare invece: invece sono rimasto a casa.

sentences.usage: Explaining why you are still in town when everybody expected you to be away.

sentences.display: Se avessi avuto tempo, sarei venuto anche io
sentences.cue: If I had had time, I would have come too
sentences.literal: If I-had had time, I-would-be come also I

words.note: avere's own participle, so avessi avuto is had had — the doubling English does too. It is regular in shape even though avere is not.

words.cue: I would have, for essere verbs
words.note: L3-M4's sarebbe is the lui cell of this same set. The participle after it agrees: sarei venuto, sarei venuta.

sentences.trap: anche io is the ordinary spoken form and needs no me. Italian keeps the subject pronoun here because anche is leaning on it, which is one of the few places a pro-drop language puts one back.
sentences.sound: se a-VES-see a-VOO-to TEM-po, sa-RAY ve-NOO-to AN-ke EE-o. anche has a hard k, AN-ke.

variations.display: Se avessi avuto tempo, sarei venuto anche oggi
variations.cue: If I had had time, I would have come today as well
variations.changed: oggi, so it is about today rather than about me

variations.display: Se avessi avuto tempo, avrei fatto tutto
variations.cue: If I had had time, I would have done everything
variations.changed: avrei fatto, an avere verb on the right

variations.display: Se avessi avuto tempo, sarei venuto ieri
variations.cue: If I had had time, I would have come yesterday
variations.changed: ieri, pinning the missed occasion

mistake.display: Se avrei avuto tempo, sarei venuto anche io
mistake.why: Again the conditional on the wrong side. se takes avessi avuto; sarei venuto is the half that gets the conditional.

sentences.usage: Turning down an invitation after the event, and meaning it.
sentences.mnemonic: Left side avessi, right side sarei.
